title: Check Point Research Tracks 2,000+ Servers Using ARTEX AI Hacking Tool
summary:
Security researchers identified a sprawling network of infrastructure used to deploy the ARTEX framework, an AI-driven tool that automates the process of penetrating computer networks. By analyzing more than 2,000 of these servers, Check Point obtained conversation logs that reveal how these autonomous agents conduct reconnaissance and establish access to target environments without human intervention.

The tool has been linked by Microsoft and CrowdStrike to Chinese state-aligned hacking groups, including an entity known as Vapor Panda that targeted more than 200 organizations in 14 countries. While the software is used for offensive operations, some builds have proven insecure; a compromised Docker image for ARTEX previously left 62 internet-facing consoles open to unauthorized administrative access.

selectedTweets.text:
A China state-backed threat group is using ARTEX, the automated agentic AI penetration testing framework, to achieve remarkable speed, scale and success in a campaign that already compromised about 140 sensitive targets in 11 days, according to CrowdStrike. 

The threat group, which CrowdStrike tracks as Vapor Panda, targeted more than 200 organizations in at least 14 countries since Oct. 17, the security company said in a threat report Thursday. Targets and confirmed victims include foreign ministries, a European country’s presidency and prime minister’s office, defense and intelligence agencies; 19 U.S.-based organizations in the pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, nuclear and financial sectors; and telecom providers in the United States, Belgium and the Philippines.
